title: Discriminating test for the Stop retirement stamp before the Engram checkpoint
outcome: A test shows that Stop's retirement of a promoted receipted head (session_lifecycle.rs, the commit_locked "failed to persist stopped admission retirement") is selected by the production delta persist at the retirement commit boundary. The observation must come BEFORE the Engram checkpoint preparation re-stamps the session (engram_host_adapter.rs session_mut_by_index at checkpoint_operation, then commit_locked). It keeps the deterministic shutdown-time watermark cut (a watcher holding the test ACP runtime's turn_lifecycle mutex until the Stop's Cancel) and the queue-retirement and Rejected-receipt checks. It fails without the retirement's own stamp and passes with it, with no timing dependence. If no deterministic observation point exists without a new test hook, record that and add the smallest test-only hook at the retirement commit. The existing a_stop_retirement_reaches_the_delta_persist_before_its_checkpoint passes with and without the stamp, because the checkpoint preparation stamp masks it, so it is not discrimination evidence. Source: the stamp audit, pair-3 RED run test-95d6f099.
acceptance: Discriminating test for the Stop retirement stamp before the Engram checkpoint is done
disposal_reason: Not needed (Fable2 #1555). The Stop-retirement stamp cannot be demonstrated by a test: Engram checkpoint preparation stamps and commits the session (engram_host_adapter.rs:5609/5626) before the checkpoint request, and production persistence is an asynchronous delta wake, so neither commit was ever a durability fence before the checkpoint. The fix is reclassified F, reading-backed defence only, with the reasoning recorded on w-32a6b3d92774. Filed before #1555 arrived; cancelled on it.
